note: Player levels, XP, skills and robot upgrades. The player carries 10 parts at first (Game.BaseInventory), 15 at most with both pocket skills. Engine independent; read by Progression.cs. XP is only ever granted once per instance/definition/zone/robot (see anti_exploit). Completing a whole ordinary item definition (every copy stored) is the main source of XP; sorting single parts gives a little. All unlock levels (robot blueprints, skills, respec) are in unlocks.json. 'status' marks what the current build implements: active = effect applied in game, planned = data reserved for a later milestone (see docs/ROADMAP.md).

destination_curve.comment: Levels come only from completed storage destinations (every assigned copy stored or installed; each destination counts once per game). Completions needed to go from level L to L+1 = max(1, round(scale * coefficient * L^exponent)), level 1 -> 2 always 1; scale = the preset's completable destinations / reference_destinations (Standard 500 -> 1, Large 751 -> 1.5, Massive 1000 -> 2). Level 25 needs about 83% of the destinations on every preset.

xp_curve.comment: Legacy: XP is still counted (telemetry, workshop score) but no longer raises the level.

levels.comment: Two points per level (three at 5, 10, 15, 20 and 23-25, the levels without a new blueprint or skill): player skills and the five robot upgrade trees share the pool, and there are more ranks than points on purpose (choices matter).

half_definition_note: Partial set credit: when half of a definition's copies (sets of 2+) are stored, this share of its completion XP is paid at once; the rest on completion (total unchanged). Gives set-focused play a moderate, not a large, head start (tools/audit/progression_sim.py: Standard L19 at 51-53% of the work broad vs 39-40% set by set).

anti_exploit.comment: Picking up and dropping items never grants XP; sorting grants XP only the first time an instance is stored, so taking an item out of storage and re-storing it gives nothing.

preset_xp_scale.comment: Per-item XP shrinks with world size so level 25 is reached at a similar completion fraction in every preset. Balance target: Massive completes in ~1.8x Standard's time (items x2.44).

skills.name: Parts Organiser
skills.comment: Identical parts stack in one slot and the pockets are sorted by type. Before this every part is its own slot, in pickup order.

supermagnet.comment: Matches the held item's exact definition id; only UNSORTED instances lying in the world (state InWorld, not reserved by robots). Works on non-magnetic materials.

robot_upgrades_note: Robot upgrade trees (docs/specs/robots_and_levels.md §6-7). Bought with skill points once that robot type is operational; model-level, so every Hoverbot shares them. stat + mode: add = base + ranks * effect_per_rank; percent = base * (1 + ranks * effect_per_rank) (negative = faster for times); rank = behaviour level read by the robot's strategy. The result never exceeds the robot's permanent limits in robots.json. cost_per_rank lists the cost of each successive rank.

respec.comment: From this level the Robots screen can refund every robot upgrade point (player skills stay).

restoration.comment: Visible restoration: each zone's lamps brighten up to +lamp_boost_at_100 as the zone is restored; the lathe runs again (spindle turns, work lamp, hum) once its zone reaches machine_zone_percent.
